title: iterative-tool-fence-and-result-anchoring-protocol
creator: Liam Chen
description: Add a resilient protocol for multi-tool chaining that enforces a deterministic loop fence, anchors intermediate tool outputs for streaming responses, and provides a compatibility shim for older SDKs that may re-invoke tools incorrectly.
background: We are seeing two failure modes in complex orchestrations: (1) unbounded re-invocation loops when downstream tools trigger upstream tool calls via injected results, and (2) streaming clients receiving inconsistent incremental outputs when tool outputs are mutated during execution. Existing guardrails are ad-hoc (per-orchestrator) and don't survive cross-service fallbacks or older SDKs that lack the new execution metadata.
goals: 1) Define a minimal per-request loop-fence token and step counter that is propagated with tool calls and validated by the runtime. 2) Implement immutable result anchors for any tool output that may be streamed back to clients. 3) Provide a compatibility shim for SDKs that don't set the fence header so that the orchestrator can infer safe defaults without breaking existing customers. 4) Add telemetry to surface near-miss recursion events and impact on latency/cost.
proposal_summary: Introduce a token-based 'loop_fence' field attached to the root request and increment a 'tool_step' counter for each tool invocation. Each tool result included in the response gets an immutable anchor ID and a cryptographic checksum to support streaming resumability. If a tool attempts to call another tool with a tool_step that decreases or repeats beyond a per-request threshold, the runtime rejects the call with a structured error and a remediation hint. For older SDKs, the gateway will synthesize a fence token and attach a synthetic provenance header; this is logged and surfaced to PM/SEs so we can prioritize SDK upgrades.
design_decisions: Use a 128-bit opaque loop_fence token (uuidv7-like) to avoid coordination with customer IDs.
tool_step is a 16-bit unsigned counter to keep payload overhead small; max safe steps = 65k but we will cap to 256 by default.
Immutable result anchors are short base62 IDs and include a sha256 checksum for integrity checks in streaming resumes.
Structured errors will use existing v2 error schema with new code TOOL_LOOP_GUARD_TRIGGERED and a user_friendly_hint field.
Gateway compatibility shim must be opt-in via a runtime flag per-tenant to avoid surprising behavior in very old customers; telemetry will default-on for the first 2 weeks in canary.
Do not change existing tool API shapes; additions are via optional headers/metadata to preserve backward compatibility.
implementation_notes: Runtime: add loop_fence propagation in request context and enforce monotonic tool_step checks in the invoker layer.
Invoker: attach result_anchor and checksum to tool responses and persist anchors in in-memory anchor cache for the lifetime of the request stream (TTL = request timeout + 30s).
Optimizer: when batching tool calls, ensure tool_step is assigned deterministically by invocation order to avoid nondeterminism in retries.
SDKs: produce patches for node/python/sdk to add explicit loop_fence header and helpers to read anchor IDs in streaming responses.
Gateway: implement compatibility shim that injects loop_fence and provenance headers for incoming SDKs that lack them, gated by tenant flag.
Telemetry: add new metrics: loop_guard_trigger_count, avg_tool_steps_per_request, anchor_cache_hit_rate, streaming_resume_success_rate.
Dashboard: quick-start console card under Console > Tooling > Loop Guards for high-severity tenants.
testing_plan: Unit tests for monotonic tool_step enforcement and rejection semantics.
Integration tests simulating tool chains with cycles (A->B->A) and verifying that second attempt is rejected and error includes remediation hint.
Streaming tests: interrupt a stream mid-tool and resume using anchor ID and checksum to validate integrity and order preservation.
Compatibility tests: gateway-synthesized fence should behave identically to explicit SDK-provided fence for at least 3 vendor SDK versions.
Chaos test: inject random delays in invoker and ensure anchor cache TTL prevents accidental false positives for resumed streams.
rollout_plan: Canary: enable runtime enforcement for 5% of hostnames in staging for 48 hours; collect metrics and fatal error rates.
Beta: enable for 25% of production tenants with compatibility shim on; contact owners of tenants with injected headers.
GA: rollout to all tenants with SDK deprecation notice for synthetic shim; provide 90-day window before shim is removed.
Migration: publish SDK patches and a migration guide with sample code and troubleshooting steps.
acceptance_criteria: Loop guard rejects cycles deterministically and returns TOOL_LOOP_GUARD_TRIGGERED with remediation hint.
Streaming clients can resume mid-stream using result_anchor and checksum with >99% success in tests.
Compatibility shim produces identical runtime behavior for at least 3 tested older SDK versions and is logged when used.
Telemetry surfaces loop_guard_trigger_count and owner contact info for tenants that hit the guard more than 3 times in 24h.
No >5% regression in P50 latency for common tool-chaining workloads after enabling anchor checks in canary.
